input_visual.observed: Many cyan and violet opaque square sprites with internal X-shaped faceting conceal the plasma. User rejects visual treatment.

diagnosis.root_cause: Fragment shader gl_FragColor=vec4(lightCol,alpha) under additive gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE,gl.ONE) ignores alpha for RGB, so even 0-opacity corners add sprite colors, producing visible square quads and X highlights.
diagnosis.secondary: Facet sideCut lets tips reach sprite bounds; prior particle defaults count46 size100 brightness100 amplify artifacts.

changes: Use premultiplied sprite emission gl_FragColor=vec4(lightCol*alpha,alpha) with discard below alpha .012
Constrain facets with sideCut=max(lateral*1.13+axial*.48,axial*.98), silhouette soft edges
Reduce sprite raster footprint (9+7*random instead of 11+9)
New soft defaults: 30 motes, 60% size, 65% brightness; all sliders still fully adjustable
Preserve one WebGL program, all 3 mote styles, source plasma ray marching, shared speed/3D orbit, quality mode, old v1 JSON schema and 18+10 controls

tests.chrome_local: PASS real Chrome Windows WebGL exit 0; six materials, 390px mobile, mouse/touch, full 360 yaw, shared spin, JSON import/export, GL 0
tests.visual_smoke: WebGL screenshot shows small colored sparks, no opaque square sprite boundaries; high-density faceted test shows clipped polygons and glowing edges.
